findings.trigger: A game server that answered once is demoted after three failed live queries (note_query_failure writes supported=False, final=False, demoted=True). While it is in that 15-minute probing window the container is observed offline - the operator restarts it, which is the natural reaction to a crashed game. note_offline sees final=False and DELETES the entry (memory and file), and the demoted flag goes with it. When the container comes back the entry is rebuilt from nothing: record_result(False) reads prev={} so demoted=bool(None)=False, and after 15 minutes without an answer (a SteamCMD update on boot, a game that no longer starts) the verdict becomes final=True, supported=False, demoted=False - the ordinary 'unsupported' state. should_probe then returns False for ever ('entry.get(supported) or not entry.get(demoted)'), so a server that is KNOWN to have query support is shown as having none, permanently, with no log line and no retry - exactly the Enshrouded case the module doc says the demoted flag was introduced to prevent. Only a manual re-test in the panel rescues it.
findings.suggestion: In note_offline keep the knowledge that the server once answered: for an entry with demoted=True do not delete it but reset only the window (e.g. self._set(name, supported=False, final=False, protocol=None, port=None, probing_since=None, demoted=True)), so the eventual gave-up verdict is 'silent' (retried every DEMOTED_RETRY_SECONDS) instead of 'unsupported'. Alternatively carry demoted across the deletion in a separate in-memory set that record_result consults.

findings.trigger: record_result decides from the IN-MEMORY entry (prev = self._state.get(name)), not from the file it is about to update under the lock. Sequence: the bot's probe pass calls reload(), then probes container X (a network query, up to a full timeout); meanwhile the operator's manual re-test in the web process succeeds and record_manual_success writes {supported: True, final: True} for X; the bot's probe fails and record_result(False) runs: prev (stale) says not final, so _set writes supported=False back - and if the 15-minute window had just expired, final=True, supported=False, demoted=False, which is never probed again. The comment at :325-327 promises 'the bot never overwrites verdicts owned by the web process (manual re-test)', but the per-key read-modify-write protects only OTHER keys; for the same key the last writer wins. The panel shows the checkbox unlocked for a moment, then it locks again although the test had just proven support. Whether reload() is really called before every pass, and how long a probe takes, is in code I cannot see - the window is the probe duration.
findings.suggestion: Make the merge rule part of the mutate under the lock: in _set, read the on-disk entry inside _atomic_update and refuse to downgrade a final supported verdict (or a 'testing' entry) with a negative probe result; likewise let record_result check the freshly locked state rather than self._state.
findings.unsure_why: Depends on the caller (does it call reload() directly before each probe, how long does a probe take) and on the timing of a manual re-test; the mechanism itself is visible.

findings.trigger: set_testing (module and instance) writes only 'testing': True into the container's entry and relies on that flag staying in the file while the panel polls it for its spinner (:142-146 says the file 'carries the verdicts AND the testing flag behind the panel's re-test spinner'). The bot's _set builds a fresh dict WITHOUT a 'testing' key and replaces the whole key ('s.update({name: entry})'). So: operator clicks re-test on a still-probing container -> testing=True written -> the bot's next probe pass changes any verdict field for that container (e.g. probing_since reset after a gap, or gave_up) -> the flag is gone -> the spinner stops while the manual test is still running, and the panel shows the bot's verdict as if the test had finished. note_offline (:304) likewise pops the key and with it a testing flag that the web process set. record_manual_success later writes the real result, so the damage is a wrong interim display, not a lost verdict.
findings.suggestion: In _set's mutate, merge instead of replace: start from the on-disk entry and overwrite only the verdict fields (keep 'testing'); in note_offline, drop the verdict fields but keep a set 'testing' flag.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see how the panel reads the flag or how often it polls; the overwrite itself is certain.

findings.trigger: get_config repairs only the two global limits when they are not numbers (_without_bad_numbers). The per-action cooldown values are taken as they are: from_dict does dict(...) without int(), problems_in validates only what arrives via the POST route, and the comment at :63-66 states that until 2026-09-26 '-5, 10**9, "abc" or true went straight into channels_config.json'. An installation that still holds such a value from before that date, or a hand-edited file, passes get_config with success=True and the defaults merge keeps the bad value (saved values win). Then: a string cooldown ('"10"' or '"abc"') makes is_on_cooldown raise TypeError at :417 ('<' between float and str) on EVERY press of that button/command - the handler crashes instead of braking; a stored 10**9 blocks the button permanently with 'please wait 999999xxx seconds'; a stored 0 or negative max_*_per_minute (int() accepts them) makes _window_exceeded refuse every press after the first one in each minute - the very failure the comment describes as fixed. Nothing is logged, because get_config believes the file.
findings.suggestion: Sanitise on the read path as well: extend _without_bad_numbers (or a sibling) to drop or clamp cooldown values that are not whole numbers within COOLDOWN_RANGE and global limits outside PER_MINUTE_RANGE, with an ERROR line naming the key, so the defaults apply for exactly that entry. The POST validator already knows the ranges; reuse problems_in per key.
findings.unsure_why: The mechanics are certain; whether real installations still hold out-of-range or string values from before the validation, and whether the button handlers catch TypeError, I cannot see.

findings.trigger: problems_in checks the two numeric globals but not enabled, cooldown_message and log_violations. from_dict coerces those with bool(), and bool("false") is True. A client that sends the switches as strings (a form field, a hand-written request) posting {"global_settings": {"enabled": "false"}} passes validation, is saved as enabled: true, and spam protection stays ON although the operator turned it off - visible only when the panel is reloaded.
findings.suggestion: In problems_in, for the three boolean keys require isinstance(value, bool) when present, mirroring the whole() check for numbers.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see whether the panel's JavaScript ever sends these as strings; with JSON booleans the path is harmless.

findings.trigger: The comment at :132-138 records that _user_cooldowns is 'unguarded' and called from both the Waitress thread and the bot loop. add_user_cooldown first collects the stale keys, then deletes them one by one: two callers entering at the same moment collect the same expired key, the second 'del self._user_cooldowns[key]' raises KeyError, which escapes add_user_cooldown into the button/command handler - after the action was already performed. Rare, but a real defect the file itself names and leaves.
findings.suggestion: Use self._user_cooldowns.pop(key, None) in the cleanup, or guard _user_cooldowns with the existing _window_lock.

findings.trigger: pre_render_all_displays returns success=True as soon as processed_count > 0. With levels 1..11 requested, ten failing (e.g. no animation data) and one already cached, the result is success=True, message 'Pre-rendered display images for 1/11 levels (1 already cached)'. A caller that tests only .success believes the pre-render worked; the per-level failures are WARNING lines only. The consequence is delayed (on-demand rendering on first Discord use, which is what the pre-render exists to avoid), not a wrong image.
findings.suggestion: Return success only when every requested level was processed (processed_count == len(levels_to_process)), and carry the failed levels in the message.

findings.trigger: The cache files are written in place: _pre_render_shadow_image saves with PIL directly to shadow_path (:230), _pre_render_unlocked_image with open(path, 'wb') (:275). The first pre-render of all eleven levels runs a Python per-pixel loop per level and is slow; a container stop or crash in the middle leaves a truncated .webp. From then on _is_pre_rendering_needed sees the file exists (and no newer source PNG) and never regenerates it, and get_mech_display_image reads the truncated bytes and returns success=True - Discord shows a broken attachment for that mech level until someone calls clear_cache, which nothing visible in this section does automatically. Two concurrent on-demand renders of the same level (bot loop and web thread) can tear the file the same way.
findings.suggestion: Write to a temp name in cache_dir and os.replace() it into place (the same pattern as utils/atomic_io), or validate the cached file (Image.open/verify) before serving and regenerate on failure.
findings.unsure_why: How likely a kill during the pre-render is depends on when the startup calls it and on the image's shutdown behaviour, which I cannot see; the non-atomic write and the 'exists means valid' check are certain.

notes: game_query_support_service: (a) a web-set {'testing': True} entry for a never-probed container is migrated by _load_file to final=False, so is_supported returns False instead of None ('unknown'); whether consumers distinguish the two I cannot see. (b) _cross_process_lock is a second implementation of what utils/atomic_io.cross_process_lock does for spam_protection_service - two places that may drift apart; I cannot see the other one. (c) A failed tmp.write_text leaves query_support.json.tmp.<pid> behind (litter only). spam_protection_service: get_config reads the file on every call and is_on_cooldown triggers it three times per press, once while holding _window_lock (_minute_limit inside _window_exceeded) - a performance shape, not a defect; save_config lets a TypeError escape when channels_config.json holds a non-object at the top level (not in its except list) - loud, hand-edited files only. update_notifier: (a) when no control channel is configured at start, mark_notification_shown() marks the version with no channel list, and should_show_update_notification then answers False for good - a control channel added later never gets this version's notice; the comment at :201-204 shows this is known, so I treat it as intended and record it only. (b) channels_still_to_tell compares channel ids from control_channel_ids() with ids round-tripped through JSON; if the former are ever strings the notice is re-sent every start - depends on code I cannot see. (c) notes_for_discord drops GitHub hard line breaks (two trailing spaces are rstripped and the line is joined) and flattens nested list indentation - cosmetic. (d) _cut can keep very little text when the only newline in the first 3800 characters sits near the start (falls back to that single '\n') - extreme edge. (e) get_update_status catches JSONDecodeError/IOError but not UnicodeDecodeError, which would escape should_show_update_notification before the try in send_update_notification - loud, garbage file only. mech_display_cache_service: __init__ uses mkdir without parents=True and will raise for a non-writable /app - depends on the image; evolution_level=0 in MechDisplayCacheRequest means 'all levels' because of the falsy test at :80. services/mech/__init__.py has no names in the plan; it only re-exports.
